clue.text: Firm with guarantee to pocket millions via media

definitions.note: Latin for 'the middle way', a course between two extremes

indicators.note: the firm and the guarantee together pocket, i.e. take inside them, the letter for millions

parts.note: a promise is a pledge or guarantee

explanation.surface: A company with a cast-iron guarantee to make millions out of the media.
explanation.walkthrough: 'via media' reads as 'through the newspapers and TV', but it is a Latin phrase meaning a middle road between extremes.
explanation.definitionFit: A middle course between two opposing positions is exactly what a settlement giving ground on both sides amounts to.

clue.text: Pots old Scots will break in scorn after cooking

indicators.note: the Scots word forces its way into the middle of the jumbled letters
once cooked, the letters of scorn are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
auld is the Scots word for old, as in Auld Lang Syne

explanation.surface: Old Scottish pots will crack, treated with contempt after a spell of cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Cauldrons are large metal cooking vessels, i.e. a kind of big pot hung over a fire.

clue.text: Mike has second child — it's a girl!

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Abel was the second son of Adam and Eve

explanation.surface: A proud announcement: Mike's partner has had their second baby, a daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Mabel is a traditional female given name, so it is an example of a girl's name.

clue.text: Gave a make-over to star back in short grass skirts

indicators.note: the grass skirts, goes around, the star and the letter

parts.note: reed is a tall waterside grass
a nova is a star that suddenly brightens

indicators.note: the back of the word short is its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A makeover sees a celebrity back in a short grass skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short grass skirts' reads as hula costume; 'short' is only where one letter comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: To renovate is to restore or refurbish, so this is the past tense meaning gave something a fresh look.

clue.text: Blues really gutted after playing semi

indicators.note: the remains of 'really' come after the rearranged letters
playing about with the letters of semi rearranges them

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a gutted word has its insides removed, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: only the first and last letters of really survive the gutting

explanation.surface: A football fan is utterly gutted after their team, Blues, played in a semi-final.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blues' looks like a team's nickname, but it is the definition: sadness.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the blues means feeling low and unhappy, which is wretchedness or unhappiness.

clue.text: Insult head of state no longer of lesser importance

parts.note: a slight is a snub or insult
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the British monarch until her death in 2022

explanation.surface: Someone insults a former head of state who is no longer so important.
explanation.definitionFit: Slight means minor or trivial, and the comparative describes something of smaller significance.

clue.text: Fish I see behind ebbing river

indicators.note: the exclamation comes behind, after, the reversed river
an ebbing tide flows back, so the river's name is read backwards

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
'Ah' is what you say when you understand: 'I see'

explanation.surface: Someone spots a fish in the shallows as the river's water level drops.
explanation.definitionFit: The opah, or moonfish, is a large brightly coloured ocean species, so it is an example of the general class.

clue.text: Presents reasons for banking some cash

indicators.note: the reasons hold the cash inside them, as a bank holds money

parts.note: pros are arguments in favour
a pound is a unit of British money

explanation.surface: Someone gives arguments in favour of putting a bit of money in the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: To propound an idea is to put it forward for consideration, i.e. offer it to others.

clue.text: Damages from hydrogen bombs etc

parts.note: arms are weapons, bombs being one example

explanation.surface: Damages caused by hydrogen bombs and other weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: To damage something is to hurt or injure it, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: Feeling much excitement, try silver rings

indicators.note: the silver's symbol rings, encircles, the attempt

parts.note: to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: An eager shopper tries on silver rings with great excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog means eagerly expectant, keyed up with curiosity or anticipation.

clue.text: You read out article about R&B style of music

indicators.note: the letters for 'you' and the article go about, around, the music genre
spoken aloud, the word you is a single letter

parts.note: the pronoun as written, before it is spoken
'an' is the indefinite article
rhythm and blues, written without its ampersand

explanation.surface: Someone reads out an article on rhythm and blues as a style of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban is a radio and record-industry label for a genre of Black popular music including hip-hop and contemporary soul.

clue.text: Way to get in side blocking crosses from the right

indicators.note: the side sits in the way of, inside, the reversed crosses
reading from the right means reading the word backwards in an across answer

parts.note: a rood is a cross or crucifix, especially in a church
a wing is a side of a building or a team's flank

explanation.surface: A football scene: a winger's side cuts out crosses coming in from the right flank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side' and 'crosses' sound like football, but crosses are church roods here.
explanation.definitionFit: A door hinged to swing both ways is one means of entrance into a room or building.

clue.text: Abused turning round in part of theatre, perform well

indicators.note: turning a word means reading it the other way round

parts.note: to revile someone is to abuse them verbally

indicators.note: the round letter is placed inside the theatre area

parts.note: 'the gods' is the highest gallery in a theatre
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A performer who has been heckled turns things round from the stage and puts on a good show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like part of 'turning round', but it is the letter shaped like a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to do what is expected or promised, i.e. succeed and come up with the results.

clue.text: Significant number frequently not finishing drinks

indicators.note: the shortened word drinks in, swallowing the number
the word for frequently stops short of its final letter

parts.note: often means frequently

explanation.surface: A worrying number of people frequently leave their drinks unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: Something notable or important deserves attention, which is what the phrase means as an adjective.

clue.text: Feeling less good about race, not content in site of rallies

indicators.note: the words for feeling less and good go about, around, the shortened race

parts.note: number means more numb, having less feeling

indicators.note: a word without its content keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone feels worse about a race and is unhappy at the track where rallies are held.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rallies' suggests motor sport, but these are the Nazi party rallies.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bavarian city hosted the huge Nazi party rallies of the 1930s, so it is famous as their venue.

clue.text: Family including Dutch guy hugged by Spice Girl roughly

indicators.note: the guy is held in the arms of, inside, the Spice Girl

parts.note: Geri Halliwell was Ginger Spice in the pop group the Spice Girls
a guy is a man
c., circa, means roughly or approximately

explanation.surface: A Dutch bloke gets a rough sort of hug from a Spice Girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch guy' reads as one man, but 'Dutch' belongs to the definition and the guy is just MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Dutch belongs to the Germanic branch of languages, together with English, German and the Scandinavian tongues.

clue.text: Works on performing Annie for ages

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first part sits on top of the second

parts.note: a mill is a factory or works

indicators.note: performing a show reworks it, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A theatre company has been working on a production of the musical Annie for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Millennia are periods of a thousand years, so they are huge stretches of time.

clue.text: Draft received by president who may put a cabinet together

definitions.text: who may put a cabinet together

indicators.note: the draft is received, taken in, by the president

parts.note: Jimmy Carter was the 39th US president
to pen something is to write or draft it

explanation.surface: A document is received by a president who can assemble a cabinet of ministers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cabinet' suggests a president's ministers, but it is a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodworker builds furniture such as cupboards, so is one who might assemble one.

clue.text: Take a holiday to the north with con artist

indicators.note: in a down answer, going north means reading upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: R stands for recipe, Latin for 'take', on prescriptions
taken as written
Noel is Christmas, a holiday
to do someone is to swindle or con them

explanation.surface: Someone takes a holiday up north with a con artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'con artist' reads as a swindler, but the two words split.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci, painter of the Mona Lisa, is the best-known Renaissance painter of that name.

clue.text: Don't say anything more left-wing? This could prevent secrets getting out

definitions.text: This could prevent secrets getting out

parts.note: 'Sh!' is a call for silence
red means left-wing, so redder is more so

explanation.surface: A plea for silence before someone says anything even more socialist.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that cuts confidential papers into strips stops sensitive information from leaking.

clue.text: Stuffier Conservative, one destined for failure

parts.note: a loser is someone fated to fail

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on a stuffy Tory politician who is doomed to lose.
explanation.definitionFit: Close weather or air is humid and airless, so the comparative describes a room even more oppressive.

clue.text: Arrested by police, hands over wine

indicators.note: the hands and over are held, arrested, inside the police

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
R and L are the right and left hands
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Someone arrested by the police hands over a bottle of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Merlot is a red grape variety and the wine made from it, so it is an example of the drink.

clue.text: Amended broadcast mean about English comic figure

indicators.note: seed broadcast is scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the mean goes about, around, the letter for English

parts.note: the average is the arithmetic mean

explanation.surface: A transmission is revised, being nasty about an English entertainer.
explanation.walkthrough: Dame Edna Everage was the drag character of the Australian comedian Barry Humphries.
explanation.definitionFit: The character was a long-running comedy creation, a gaudy self-important Melbourne housewife turned superstar.

clue.text: Daily Record's rising support on line

indicators.note: in a down answer, rising means read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: aid is help or support
RY is a railway, a line

explanation.surface: The Scottish newspaper Daily Record has growing backing online.
explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Record is a Scottish tabloid newspaper; here it just means a record kept every day.
explanation.definitionFit: A journal in which one writes an entry each day is a day-by-day account.

clue.text: Public display from unclothed, attractive person

indicators.note: the word's outer covering, its first and last letters, is taken off

parts.note: a sexpot is a sexually attractive person

explanation.surface: An attractive person strips off in public.
explanation.definitionFit: An expo is an exposition, a large exhibition open to the public.

clue.text: Worry covers ripped off rap music

indicators.note: the outer letters, the word's covers, are torn away

parts.note: gangsta is a style of rap music

explanation.surface: Fear that rap music recordings, its covers, are being plagiarised.
explanation.definitionFit: Angst is a German loanword for dread or anxiety, a general feeling of unease.

clue.text: Out of time in advanced test that overwhelms worker

indicators.note: the advanced test swallows up, holds inside it, the worker

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam
a temp is a temporary worker

explanation.surface: A candidate runs out of time in a tough advanced exam that defeats a staff member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of time' looks like a clock running down, but it is the definition: standing outside time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something atemporal exists independently of time, untouched by its passage.

clue.text: Lean back, welcoming good time for a rest

indicators.note: the reversed word welcomes the letter in, holding it inside
lean back means the synonym for lean is read backwards

parts.note: thin means lean, skinny

explanation.surface: An instruction to recline and enjoy a pleasant moment of relaxation.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours of darkness are when people normally sleep, so it is the period set aside for resting.

clue.text: This requires you to do a stretch in Tokyo gaol

definitions.text: This requires you to do a stretch

indicators.note: the answer is found in the letters of the two words that follow

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of Tokyo and the start of gaol

explanation.surface: A prisoner in a Japanese jail is made to serve time, a stretch, and exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do a stretch' is slang for serve a prison sentence, which the gaol encourages.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian discipline is built on postures that lengthen and extend the body's muscles.

clue.text: When doctorate's done by mostly serious man of letters

parts.note: a doctorate is normally taken after a master's degree, i.e. post-MA

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: stern means serious, severe

explanation.surface: An academic, doctorate finished, becomes a rather solemn writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man of letters' suggests a writer, but this one handles the mail.
explanation.definitionFit: The person in charge of a post office deals with people's mail, so is a man of letters in the postal sense.
